x: C is right: the Assam Movement (led by AASU) was an Assamese-Bengali conflict over illegal migration. A is the Manipur Meitei-Kuki conflict over ST status, B the Mizo-Bru conflict (not about the Eighth Schedule), and D the Tripura tribes-vs-Bengali-settlers conflict.

The Sixth Schedule, under Article 244(2), provides autonomous district councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. Article 244(1) relates to the Fifth Schedule (Scheduled Areas elsewhere), and Article 371 contains special provisions for particular States.
The Scheduled Areas of Andhra Pradesh cover 16,267.63 sq km, about 10.15% of the State's area, with 3,512 villages; about 12.9 lakh tribals live in them.

B is right: retaliatory communalism attempts to harm members of other communities (riots, revenge cycles). A is wrong: welfarist communalism works for one community's welfare; using religion for votes is political communalism. C is wrong: keeping away from politics is retreatist. D is wrong: seeking an independent state outside India is secessionist.

A is the wrongly matched pair: Jinnah issued his Fourteen Points in 1929 in reply to the Nehru Report (1928); 1940 is the year of the Lahore ('Pakistan') Resolution (24 March 1940). The Communal Award (1932, Ramsay MacDonald) and Iqbal's 1930 proposal for a consolidated Muslim state are correctly dated.
